description: FIRST_VALUE / LAST_VALUE null treatment: the default is RESPECT NULLS - the first or last row's value, even when it is NULL - where the engine previously skipped NULLs unconditionally. The IGNORE NULLS modifier selects the first or last non-null value, and RESPECT NULLS is also accepted explicitly. Over the frame (1,NULL),(2,20),(3,30),(4,NULL) with a whole-partition window, every row sees first=NULL and last=NULL by default, 20 and 30 under IGNORE NULLS, and a column with no nulls behaves as a plain first and last. Converted 1:1 from functions/FirstLastValueNullsTest (now retired); its @BeforeEach fixture is inlined per test and the Java helper's read of the first output row becomes a LIMIT 1 over the same ordered query.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO w VALUES (1, NULL), (2, 20), (3, 30), (4, NULL)
SELECT r FROM (SELECT id, FIRST_VALUE(v) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS r FROM w ORDER BY id) LIMIT 1
CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO w VALUES (1, NULL), (2, 20), (3, 30), (4, NULL)
SELECT r FROM (SELECT id, FIRST_VALUE(v) IGNORE NULLS OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS r FROM w ORDER BY id) LIMIT 1
CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO w VALUES (1, NULL), (2, 20), (3, 30), (4, NULL)
SELECT r FROM (SELECT id, FIRST_VALUE(v) RESPECT NULLS OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS r FROM w ORDER BY id) LIMIT 1
CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO w VALUES (1, NULL), (2, 20), (3, 30), (4, NULL)
SELECT r FROM (SELECT id, LAST_VALUE(v) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS r FROM w ORDER BY id) LIMIT 1
CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO w VALUES (1, NULL), (2, 20), (3, 30), (4, NULL)
SELECT r FROM (SELECT id, LAST_VALUE(v) IGNORE NULLS OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS r FROM w ORDER BY id) LIMIT 1
CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO w VALUES (1, NULL), (2, 20), (3, 30), (4, NULL)
SELECT r FROM (SELECT id, FIRST_VALUE(id) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS r FROM w ORDER BY id) LIMIT 1
